title: DOACs for Mitral Regurgitation: A Long-Term Follow-up
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral Regurgitation represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. DOACs has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in mitral regurgitation. METHODS: We conducted a long-term follow-up involving 2,500 participants with confirmed mitral regurgitation (mean age 55 years, 63% male). Participants were randomized to receive either doacs or standard care. The primary endpoint was composite clinical endpoint. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 11 months. RESULTS: Treatment with doacs resulted in a 19% relative improvement in composite clinical endpoint versus standard care (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.6-0.84, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 42 percentage points (NNT = 20). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 41% of the treatment group versus 32% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 10% and 9% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for mitral regurgitation, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of doacs into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
